title: Heart Failure: Reduced Versus Preserved Ejection Fraction
subject: Medicine
preview: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction involves systolic pump impairment; preserved ejection fraction involves elevated filling pressures despite non-reduced EF.
quickRevision: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction involves systolic pump impairment; preserved ejection fraction involves elevated filling pressures despite non-reduced EF.
Echocardiography helps classify EF, structural disease and filling abnormalities.
Treatment strategies differ by phenotype, congestion, cause and comorbidities; diagnosis is not based on EF alone.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction involves systolic pump impairment; preserved ejection fraction involves elevated filling pressures despite non-reduced EF.
Symptoms can include dyspnea, orthopnea, edema and exercise intolerance across phenotypes.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A normal-range EF does not exclude clinical heart failure.
